ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Member of Technical Staff, Modeling in Harvey Research, you’ll own how we adapt and improve leading open-weight models for legal work.

We recently post-trained our first model built for legal work, and we’re now building the team to scale up our post-training efforts. You’ll own the post-training recipe across SFT and RL, including reward design and verification for challenging, semi-verifiable legal tasks. You’ll help set the research direction and carry ideas from experiments through training runs to models used by customers. You’ll join a small, high-bar team of hands-on engineers and researchers, where each person owns a large part of the work.

We’re looking for research engineers and scientists who have gotten training runs working at scale, are immersed in RL for language models, and want their work to reach users quickly.

Learn more about our work at harvey.ai/research http://harvey.ai/research.

 - Own and pursue a research agenda to improve model capability on long-horizon legal reasoning and agentic workflows.

 - Design and run post-training experiments across SFT and RL, building on leading open-weight models.

 - Develop reward functions and verifiers for semi-verifiable tasks, including rubrics, learned preference models, and expert preference data, and study where they break.

 - Run and debug training at scale, addressing divergence, reward hacking, and instability.

 - Build and use rigorous evals to track improvements and decide what ships.

 - Design, implement, test, and debug code across our research stack.




WHAT YOU HAVE

 - Hands-on experience post-training LLMs with SFT and RL, including preference optimization, and direct ownership of training runs and results.

 - Deep ML fundamentals and experience getting distributed training runs working reliably.

 - Strong engineering skills in Python, with production-quality code and end-to-end system ownership.

 - Research experience in RL for language models or reward modeling, with the ability to move quickly from experiments to shipped improvements. Publications welcome, not required.

We are hiring for this role across multiple levels.




COMPENSATION

$230,000 - $450,000 USD

SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.
About the Team
The compiler team at SambaNova powers the RDU through a unique compilation strategy. By fusing kernels into dataflow graphs that run across the entire accelerator architecture, we avoid sequential kernel launches and eliminate the memory traffic that bottlenecks conventional hardware. This is a key differentiator and unlike any other product on the market.
About the Role
As a new grad Compiler Engineer, you'll work on core areas of our compiler, including the IR and pass infrastructure, model lowering and partitioning, tensor tiling, memory management, and mapping operations onto the fabric. Compiler and hardware design are closely linked here, and you'll see how compiler decisions affect chip performance. You'll write production code in C++ and Python, debug at a low level, and work with the runtime and hardware teams. Senior engineers will review your code and mentor you as you take on larger parts of the compiler.
Responsibilities
Implement and optimize passes in the compiler's IR and pass infrastructure
Lower and partition machine learning models for execution on the RDU
Develop tensor tiling and memory management for on-chip memory
Map operations onto the RDU fabric to improve model performance
Debug compiler and performance issues at a low level in C++ and Python
Required Qualifications
B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field
Experience in machine learning systems development, including ML compilers, LLM inference kernels, or kernel generation
Strong programming skills in Python and C/C++
Experience programming GPUs or other AI accelerators
Preferred Qualifications
M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field
Experience with ML compiler frameworks such as MLIR or StableHLO
Experience with LLM kernel libraries
Machine learning systems research experience
Open source project ownership or contributions
Experience building AI agent driven tools or automation
